correctness.rationale: Right evaluation at D=diag(a_1,...,a_n) gives f(D)_{ij}=p_{ij}(a_j), so finite-field scalar factorization yields the exact column-divisibility null ideal. Equal projection polynomials make it a full matrix ideal. Conversely, right multiplication by a matrix unit moves a generator h_j from column j into column k, forcing h_k|h_j; symmetry and monicity force equality for all j,k. Inclusion-exclusion over omitted coordinate-symbol pairs gives the count, and a union bound gives the asymptotic estimate. I independently recomputed the formula values 10, 196, 63778, 290 and 42610 for the five verifier parameter pairs, agreeing with the frozen verifier; those finite checks are corroborative only.

final_claim: For every finite diagonal subset S of M_n(F), its null ideal is exactly the set of polynomial matrices whose j-th column is divisible by the vanishing polynomial of the j-th coordinate projection; hence S is core iff all coordinate projections coincide. Over F_q this gives the stated exact inclusion-exclusion count and core proportion at least 1-nq*2^{-q^(n-1)}.
scientific_limitations: An equivalent diagonal-set result may occur in integer-valued-polynomial literature without the term 'core set'.
The structural criterion assumes simultaneous diagonal form over the ground field; it does not classify nondiagonalizable commuting sets or arbitrary matrix subsets.
